description: Bench-top photograph (no axes, no scale bar) laid out as three vertical columns of specimens above a straight ruler whose printed graduations run 16 to 29, one unit apart. In each column the top object is a warm-forged steel billet and the two objects beneath it are machined tensile specimens cut from that billet. The billets are dark, oxidised and heavily distorted: the left billet is the least deformed with a rounded, barrelled, roughly rectangular profile; the middle billet is taller and clearly shows the X-shaped/sheared deformation pattern of multiaxial forging with edge barrelling; the right billet shows the strongest distortion, with sheared corners and flaking/spalled surface scale. Each billet carries a hand-scratched pass marking, legible in reading order as "1X", "3X" and "5X", so the columns correspond left-to-right to MAF-1, MAF-3 and MAF-5. The six tensile specimens are cylindrical with turned, threaded grip ends and a reduced gauge section, their surfaces dark grey/black oxidised; two samples per billet were cut out. Against the ruler the leftmost billet spans roughly the 16-to-19.5 graduations, the middle about 21 to 24, and the right about 25.5 to 28.5. The figure documents the outward geometry and survivability of the forged billets and the tensile blanks extracted from them.
measured_quantities: billet dimension along the ruler scale (printed graduations 16 to 29; unit not labelled in the image)

observations.observation: The image is a photograph of three forged billets arranged left to right, each with two machined tensile specimens placed directly below it, giving three sample columns in total.
Hand-scratched markings on the billets read, in reading order, "1X", "3X" and "5X", identifying the columns by MAF pass number.
The billets are dark and oxidised, and the distortion increases from left to right: the left billet is only mildly barrelled, while the right billet shows sheared corners and flaked surface scale.
The middle and right billets show an X-shaped deformation pattern with bulged edges, consistent with multiaxial forging.
The six tensile specimens are cylindrical with turned, threaded grip ends and a reduced gauge section, with dark grey to black oxidised surfaces.
A ruler is laid along the bottom of the frame with printed graduations numbered 16 through 29, the digits increasing left to right.

The billets sit at different positions along the ruler: the leftmost billet spans approximately the 16.5 to 19.5 graduations, the middle billet about 21 to 24, and the right billet about 25.5 to 28.5.
The caption states the figure shows the forged billets and the cutout tensile samples after MAF-1, MAF-3 and MAF-5.
The citing text defines the sample notation MAF-0, MAF-1, MAF-3 and MAF-5 for the initial annealed state (0 pass) and one, three and five MAF passes respectively.
The citing text states the sample could only be forged a total of five times before breaking on the sixth attempt, which is why the photograph contains no MAF-6 billet.
The citing text states the processed samples at 0, 1, 3 and 5 passes accumulated 33% normal strain per pass.

The citing text notes that simulation (Fig. 12) does not accurately reproduce the experimental distortion in the shape of the specimens shown here, and attributes this to the absence of crystallographic texture effects in the simulation.
No tension-test data, fracture surfaces or micrographs appear in this figure; it is purely a macroscopic record of billet shape and specimen preparation.

subfigures.description: Leftmost column: a dark, oxidised warm-forged billet with a rounded, slightly barrelled profile, hand-marked "1X", sitting above two machined cylindrical tensile specimens with threaded grip ends and reduced gauge sections cut from it. Corresponds to MAF-1.

Middle column: a taller forged billet marked "3X" showing pronounced edge barrelling and an X-shaped deformation pattern typical of multiaxial forging, with two cut-out tensile specimens of the same design beneath it. Corresponds to MAF-3.

Rightmost column: the most severely deformed forged billet, marked "5X", with sheared corners and patches of flaked/spalled surface oxide, and two cut-out tensile specimens beneath it. Corresponds to MAF-5.
